label: L=9, second copy step (t=10), favouring first token l/z
explanation: Very sparse (about 0.03% of steps). Every activation on dev is at one position: length-9 sequences at t=10 (recall_idx=1, the step right after <DEL> where orig(0) is fed back and orig(1) is output). That position predicate gets recall and mass recall of 1.0, but only 2.4% of such steps fire, so which ones do is token-dependent. The strongest modulator is the fed-back first token: l and z (about 8x lift, 59% of mass together), then w, n, c, 3. Output token z/3/b raises the rate too, but the effect is weaker and spread out. The top activations are mostly l- or z-initial sequences. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, for any other L, or at any other copy step. Restricting to l/z raises precision to about 18% but drops recall to about 51%; the remaining selectivity is spread across tokens and was not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig4=w (+2.31), orig3=w (+2.15), L=9 & t=10 (+1.92), t=10 & prev_tok=<DEL> (+1.92), L=9 & recall_idx=1 (+1.92), t=10 & in_tok=l (+1.74). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.30), prev2_tok=w (-2.03), orig3=y (-1.70), prev2_tok=c (-1.59).
